dossier.public_summary: The dip alternates deep and shallow every 14.4 days and individual transits vary by more than an order of magnitude, with two outliers creating the signal. This depth alternation and inconsistency are better explained by an eclipsing binary or a few spurious dips than by a steady planet transit.

reasons.why: Large odd/even difference with same sign in all sectors (sector_oe_same_sign_share 1) and depth ratio 3.8 and difference 3688 ppm points to a binary at twice the period (28.8 d) rather than alternation noise; seen in sector_oe_max_sigma 6.774 and cross-sector consistency.

Individual transit depths are wildly inconsistent with a single depth, with two extreme outliers driving the signal and SNR 10.36 low-SNR detection that is not a steady transit, favouring a few bad/fake events over a planet.

reasons.why: Flat-ish shape and no plausible neighbour within one pixel and centroid inconclusive do not outweigh the positive odd-even and depth-variability evidence, which together positively favour an eclipsing binary/false alarm over a planet.
